title: Shared-result ritual
summary: Build a shared-result surface with waiting, interruption, reveal, and selected states.
originNote: Distilled from a recurring history-derived interest in staging chance, waiting, and consequence as a coherent ritual.

setup.instructions: Mount the fictional event packet and validator. Build a self-contained runnable artifact with no network calls or external media. Copy or embed every runtime input the artifact needs into the allowed published output paths; fixtures/ and validation/ are not shipped with the Dish.

turns.content: Read fixtures/event.json and build a complete responsive result surface as index.html. Let a reviewer enter waiting, interrupted, sealed, reveal, and selected states without navigation or reload. Prefer ordinary product interactions; if the natural flow does not expose every state, put the remaining controls in a clearly labelled Review states panel kept separate from the main ritual. Show the packet's exact message for the active state and expose state changes through an appropriate live region. Treat the drawing as a room of people awaiting one consequential moment rather than a metrics dashboard. Derive the visual register from the event. Motion, copy, type, and sound-free feedback may be expressive only when they clarify anticipation, interruption, verification, reveal, or consequence. Preserve the eventful register without adding ornamental spectacle. Every state must remain distinct under prefers-reduced-motion. Do not invent money, gambling, accounts, prizes, testimonials, or participant details beyond the packet.

checks.description: The entry and any shipped JavaScript or stylesheet assets are nonempty, and JavaScript parses as modules.
In a browser, activate waiting, interrupted, sealed, reveal, and selected without reload; verify the exact messages, live announcements, reduced-motion behavior, and keyboard-only operation.
